chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā, from al-Washshā’, from Hammād ibn ‘Uthmān, from Sa‘īd Bayyā‘ al-Sābirī, who said:
I said to Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: “May a man force himself to weep in salat (prayer)?” He said: “Excellent, excellent, even if it be like the head of a fly.”

key_terms.بَخٍ بَخٍ: an expression of praise and approval
key_terms.رَأْسِ اَلذُّبَابِ: the head of a fly; a metaphor for something extremely small
key_terms.يَتَبَاكَى: to make oneself weep or induce the appearance/state of crying

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to make oneself weep during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates approval of inducing a state of weeping in salat (prayer), even if the outward sign is extremely slight. It points to the value of humility, softness of heart, and khushu‘ during worship.
